key_insight: Precursor-ratio control of chloride vacancies enables forming-free, gradual resistive switching in lead-free KCuCl3−x memristors for neuromorphic learning, rather than solar-cell applications.
engineering_relevance: Tuning vacancy concentration balances ionic mobility and defect controllability, offering a materials-design route to reliable analog synapses.
method: Vary precursor ratios during wet-chemical synthesis to tune chloride vacancies.
Evaluate defect-dependent electronic structure and switching in W/KCuCl3−x/FTO memristors.
Use measured conductance characteristics as synaptic weights in neural-network simulations.
evidence_signal: At an optimal vacancy concentration of approximately 1.3 × 10^21 cm−3, devices show highly linear potentiation/depression and pulse endurance above 10^4 cycles; simulations achieve 98.96% MNIST and 91.82% Fashion-MNIST accuracy.
watch_item: Recognition results are simulation-based; the abstract does not establish array-scale hardware accuracy, energy consumption, or long-term retention.
paper_title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
